title: Investigating the Contribution of Socio-Physical Structure of Neighborhoods on Residents' Sense of Attachment
research_question:
1. To what extent do the social and physical factors contribute to residents' satisfaction with their neighborhoods?
2. Which of the social and physical factors plays the more significant role in creating an attachment to the neighborhood?

participants.description: 180 residents (93 men, 87 women, mean age=35 years) from 4 neighborhoods in Karaj, Iran. Each neighborhood had n=45 participants. Most owned their homes (68.75%) and had a master's degree (47.5%).
participants.recruitment: Randomly selected using a cluster sampling method, volunteered to participate through door-to-door visits.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: Four distinct residential neighborhoods in Karaj, Iran: Azimiyeh (N1), Owj (N2), Baghestan (N3), and Baraghan (N4). These neighborhoods differed in settlement date, size, available services, and urban context.

findings.quote: the differences in the degree of place attachment indicate the influence of social and physical factors.
compared to the physical dimension, the social dimension plays a stronger role.
factors such as social interactions and easy access to amenities directly contribute to residents' attachment
factors such as social interactions and easy access to amenities directly contribute to residents' attachment
other factors have an indirect effect on attachment, such as order and maintenance
other factors have an indirect effect on attachment, such as order and maintenance, attitudes toward the neighborhood
other factors have an indirect effect on attachment, such as order and maintenance, attitudes toward the neighborhood, and public participation in the neighborhood.
The attitudinal attachment variable indirectly affects the sense of attachment to the neighborhood through the social engagement variable.
Both variables, participation, and order affect attachment to the neighborhood through the physical potential variable.
Both variables, participation, and order affect attachment to the neighborhood through the physical potential variable.
the culture and values variable not only directly affects sense of attachment but also has an impact on the social engagement variable and indirectly affects the sense of attachment indirectly.

findings.consequent: Access to public spaces and facilities

mechanisms: Social engagement mediates the effect of attitudinal attachment and culture & values on neighborhood attachment.
Physical potentials mediate the effect of participation and order on neighborhood attachment.
implementation_implications: To create more efficient places, it is necessary to understand the different meanings that a neighborhood has for its residents.
Designing high-quality public spaces and making them accessible to all can improve place attachment and resident satisfaction.
Promoting social interactions and community activities can enhance place attachment.
Addressing physical conditions like order, maintenance, and safety can indirectly improve attachment.

limitations: The study was limited to 4 neighborhoods in Karaj, Iran, which may not be generalizable to other contexts.
The sample size of 180 participants, with 45 per neighborhood, might be small for complex statistical analyses.
The study relied heavily on self-report questionnaires, which may be subject to social desirability bias.
The cross-sectional design does not allow for causal inferences, only associations.
The study did not explicitly measure all potential mediating or moderating variables that could influence place attachment.
